hints: Focus on counting carbons, the acid part must come from the correct part of the starting molecule.
Remember that acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile with formula R-CN gives the carboxylic acid R-COOH with the same carbon count.
Check what each ester and nitrile would actually give, and remember alkaline hydrolysis of an ester gives a salt, not the free acid.
walkthrough:
**What is our target?**

Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. It has 3 carbons in total. So we need a reaction that makes this exact 3-carbon acid.

Target:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Recall the two hydrolysis routes**

For esters, acidic hydrolysis gives carboxylic acid + alcohol. Alkaline hydrolysis gives carboxylate salt + alcohol, not the free acid.

For nitriles, acidic hydrolysis gives carboxylic acid + ammonium ion:
$$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+, \text{heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Test each starting material**

Propyl ethanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The acyl part is 2 carbons, so it gives ethanoic acid, not propanoic acid.

Ethyl propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It has the right 3-carbon acyl part, but alkaline conditions give propanoate ion, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$, plus ethanol.

Ethanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ (2 carbons), so it gives ethanoic acid.

**Pick the match**

Propanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ (3 carbons). Acidic hydrolysis keeps all 3 carbons and forms the -COOH group:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
This is exactly propanoic acid.

options.A: Acidic hydrolysis of propyl ethanoate gives ethanoic acid plus propan-1-ol. The acid comes from the ethanoate part (2 carbons), so you get $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, not propanoic acid. Trap is looking at the propyl alcohol part instead of the acid part.
options.B: Alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl propanoate does contain the propanoyl group, but with NaOH it gives sodium propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$, plus ethanol. You do not get the free propanoic acid unless you then acidify. Trap is forgetting alkaline means salt product.
options.C: Propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, has 3 carbons. Acidic hydrolysis converts the -CN group directly into -COOH, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ which is propanoic acid plus $\text{NH}_4^+$. Carbon count is preserved, so this is correct.
options.D: Acidic hydrolysis of ethanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$, gives ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, because the nitrile has only 2 carbons. Trap is forgetting that nitrile hydrolysis keeps the same number of carbons, so a 2-carbon nitrile cannot make a 3-carbon acid.
